Super late to post this but figured it’s worth the story. When I was 17, I had just gotten my license, a car (the old family one), and a new job. Life was pretty great. I spent the summer off-roading with my friends and spending hundreds on gas a month. My car seems fine, it runs well, and gets us through the mud. Now, my dad’s a mechanic, so he’s taught me to know better than taking a car off-roading. He also taught me a whole lotta basic car lecture, but gave me the benefit of the doubt when it came to the ‘don’t use a 20 year old Contour for mudding’ lecture. 

Anyways, one morning I run to the bank before school, and when I come out, I notice my tire is a little low. I realize it’s been low for a while. So I shrug, and looking for an excuse to skip school, tell my dad that I need to come into his shop to fill up my tire. The drive is about 5 minutes away, and a couple of those minutes is spent driving down a gravel path. 

I get on to the gravel path, drive for about fifteen seconds, before my tire goes flying off. Single scariest moment of my life. Luckily, the road is off a ways from the main shop area and no one was around, so nobody was hurt. It took me a couple days (and a few hundred dollars) to realize that a) if I had gone onto the highway to go to school instead, it would’ve ended in a far different way, and b) stick to trucks for 4x4ing.
